doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Peanut butter on tour in Japan with Pat Boone
summary: In Japan he avoided the geisha-house fish dinner by pulling out his jar of peanut butter.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: No that’s a classic. There’s a peanut butter story too. When I went to Japan with Pat Boone and after the opening show generally in Tokyo, they take you over to this geisha place where the girls perform, you know I mean it’s not what people think, and then they serve a dinner. And they bring out these fish, blue fish and yellow fish and red fish and they’re lying on the plate looking up at you like this. And it wasn’t too appetizing. And I had this coat on with a bulge in it, and I asked the guy I said, “do you have soybean cookies?” “Oh yes.” I said, “do you have coke?” I said, “soybean cookies and a coke.” So they brought me the soybean cookies and a coke. I said, “do you have a knife?” “Yeah.” And then I whipped out my jar of Laura Scotta Peanut Butter, and that has followed me ever since. This is clear back in the mid-60s I did this. I ran into Rosie Clooney about six months later and she’d been in Japan and she said, “I heard all about your peanut butter.” Because they don’t have peanut butter over there. I mean they didn’t then. But I couldn’t eat the Japanese food so I always carried a couple of jars of peanut butter with me to get me through.
